name: Old Quarter
dotReason: Worth a special trip in this corridor
summary: Hanoi’s 36 guild streets in one square kilometre north of Hoan Kiem Lake, tube houses and street kitchens. Walk silver on Hang Bac and silk on Hang Gai, eat pho and bun cha, browse Dong Xuan, and after dark take a stool where Ta Hien meets Luong Ngoc Quyen. Weekend nights fill Hang Dao. Free to wander and best on foot.
getThere: Walk north from Hoan Kiem Lake
bestMonths: April to June, or September to December
seoTitle: Hanoi Old Quarter — 36 guild streets, street food, Ta Hien
seoDescription: Walk Hanoi’s Old Quarter: 36 guild streets of tube houses north of Hoan Kiem Lake, pho and bun cha from the street kitchens, silver on Hang Bac, and bia hoi on Ta Hien after dark.
intro: You walk into 36 guild streets packed into one square kilometre north of Hoan Kiem Lake, each still named for the trade it has carried since the 14th or 15th century: silver on Hang Bac, silk on Hang Gai, festival goods on Hang Ma, herbs on Lan Ong. The houses are tube houses, narrow shopfronts that run deep and high, with courtyards cut in for light.

Eat on the street. Pho and bun cha come out of the street kitchens in these lanes, egg coffee is the cup, and on weekend nights Hang Dao fills with food. After dark, take a plastic stool at the bia hoi corner where Ta Hien meets Luong Ngoc Quyen.

The lanes are free and open from 7am to midnight. Go in the morning, when the pavement is easier, and take a cyclo for a first look before you walk. Bach Ma, the temple at 76 Hang Buom, and Dong Xuan, the covered market at the north end, sit on the same walk. If a citadel morning is the trip, sleep elsewhere in Hanoi.
gettingAround: Walk north from Hoan Kiem Lake. Dong Xuan Market, at the far end of the lanes, is about 800 m to 2 km away on foot. Take a cyclo for a first look, then do the streets on foot.

stayAreas.name: Near Hoan Kiem
stayAreas.summary: Sleep on the lake side when you want the market and the centre of the city on one walk. Hang Dao runs north from that end into the lanes.

stayAreas.name: Hang Buom and Ma May
stayAreas.summary: Sleep on Hang Buom, Ma May, or Hang Be when the walk to Dong Xuan is the point. The evening corner, Ta Hien and Luong Ngoc Quyen, is in the same lanes.

eat: Pho and bun cha are the bowls of these lanes, and egg coffee is the cup. On weekend nights the food moves onto Hang Dao. The Hanoi food guide has the full menu.
interestsBody: Dining is pho and bun cha from the street kitchens, egg coffee, and weekend nights on Hang Dao. The Hanoi food guide is the menu.
The walk is the lanes themselves: tube houses, guild streets named for their trade, and Bach Ma on Hang Buom.
Evenings end at the bia hoi corner of Ta Hien and Luong Ngoc Quyen, on low stools in the street.
Shopping is Dong Xuan, the covered market at the north end, then the trade streets: Hang Bac for silver, Hang Gai for silk, Hang Ma for festival goods, and Lan Ong for herbs.

blocks.heading: The streets
paragraphs: The Old Quarter is one square kilometre of 36 streets north of Hoan Kiem Lake, free to enter and open from 7am to midnight. Since the 14th or 15th century each street has been named for the goods its artisans made and sold, and many still trade under those names.
Tube houses are the narrow fronts that run deep and high, with courtyards cut in for light. Take a cyclo for a first look, then walk, ideally in the morning before the pavement fills.
Bach Ma, the temple at 76 Hang Buom, is the stop on the way to Dong Xuan.

cards.title: Bach Ma Temple
cards.summary: A yellow-walled temple on Hang Buom, with dragons on the roof ridge and a white horse on the altar.

interestGroups.title: Nightlife
interestGroups.summary: Bia hoi on stools at the Ta Hien corner once the lanes go dark.

blocks.heading: Ta Hien and Luong Ngoc Quyen
paragraphs: After dark the corner of Ta Hien and Luong Ngoc Quyen is the bia hoi corner: fresh draft beer, low tables, and plastic stools pushed out into the street.
Walk there through the lanes from the lake or from Hang Buom. The quarter stays open until midnight.

cards.title: Ta Hien beer corner
cards.summary: Bia hoi on low plastic stools at Ta Hien and Luong Ngoc Quyen, the street crowded once it is dark.

interestGroups.title: Shopping
interestGroups.summary: Dong Xuan is the covered hall. The guild streets around it still sell silver, silk, festival goods, and herbs.

blocks.heading: Dong Xuan Market
paragraphs: Dong Xuan is the covered market at the north end of the lanes, on Dong Xuan street, with its management office at 1A Cau Dong. It runs over three floors: clothes and accessories on the ground floor, bolts of cloth, and a dry-goods section called Bac Qua. Come for the wholesale bustle more than for souvenirs.
The hall opens early in the morning and stays open late on Friday to Sunday. Stall hours shift around holidays and repairs, so confirm the hall is open before you make it the morning’s goal.

blocks.heading: The guild streets
paragraphs: Hang Bac is the silver street, lined with gold-and-silver shopfronts. Hang Gai sells silk. Hang Ma sells festival goods, its shopfronts hung with decorations and, at the turn of the year, stacked with Christmas and New Year stock. Lan Ong is the herb street.
Walk them as one loop from the lake and let the shopfronts decide where you stop.

blocks.heading: Weekend nights on Hang Dao
paragraphs: On weekend nights Hang Dao, the street that runs north from the lake, fills with food stalls. Eat your way up it, then cut across to Ta Hien for a beer.

cards.title: Dong Xuan Market
cards.summary: Bolts of cloth and three floors of wholesale stalls in the covered hall at the north end.

cards.title: Hang Bac
cards.summary: The silver street: jewellers’ windows and engraving shops under the old trade name.

cards.title: Hang Ma
cards.summary: The festival-goods street, its shops stacked with decorations for the season.

faqs.q: Do I need a ticket for the lanes?
faqs.a: No. The streets are free and open from 7am to midnight. Bach Ma Temple charges 20,000 VND a visit from 8 December 2025, with under-16s free. Dong Xuan Market has no entry ticket; you pay at the stalls.

In the morning, before the pavement fills. Across the year, April to June and September to December are the clearer months for Hanoi, with September to November the narrower window. June to August is hot, humid, and rainy.
Daily 08:00–12:00 and 13:30–17:30, with an evening session from 19:00 on Friday to Sunday that closes at 21:00 or 21:30. Older boards at the gate showed different hours, so read the board on the day.

season.label: Clearer walking months
season.note: Walk in April to June or September to December, and September to November if you want the narrowest window. June to August is hot, humid, and rainy: start the walk in the morning.
